description: Controlled benchmark evaluating SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct for editorial narrative-to-visual evidence auditing on standard GitHub runner

test_cases.title: Sorting Hat Beat 1 - Slytherin Consideration vs Hogwarts Lake Pan
test_cases.claim: Did you know the Sorting Hat considered placing Harry Potter in Slytherin?
test_cases.expected_location: Hogwarts castle exterior / mountains / lake landscape
test_cases.expected_action: Scenic landscape pan across mountains and water
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: The footage displays a scenic exterior camera pan of Hogwarts and a lake. No Sorting Hat is visible, Harry Potter is not visible, and no Sorting ceremony or Slytherin discussion occurs.

test_cases.title: Sorting Hat Beat 2 - Hat Placed on Head & Detected Ambition
test_cases.claim: When placed on his head, the hat detected great talent, resourcefulness, and hidden ambition.
test_cases.expected_action: The Sorting Hat is lowered onto Harry Potter's head
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: The physical action of placing the Sorting Hat onto Harry's head is directly visible. However, the internal cognitive/metaphysical detection of 'great talent, resourcefulness, and hidden ambition' is non-visual lore that cannot be directly proven by the visual frames.

test_cases.title: Sorting Hat Beat 3 - Hat Debates Out Loud vs Ollivander Wand Handover
test_cases.claim: In the book, the hat debates out loud, explicitly naming Slytherin before Harry pleads for Gryffindor.
test_cases.expected_location: Ollivanders Wand Shop in Diagon Alley
test_cases.expected_action: Ollivander handing a wand box to Harry Potter
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: CRITICAL MISMATCH: Narration discusses the Sorting Hat debating aloud between Slytherin and Gryffindor in the Great Hall, but the rendered visual is Mr. Ollivander handing Harry a wand in his Diagon Alley shop. Completely unrelated scene, location, and action.

test_cases.title: Sorting Hat Beat 4 - Hat Honours Choice vs Quidditch Snitch Catch
test_cases.claim: The hat honours his choice -- but the ambition it sensed would define his entire journey.
test_cases.expected_action: Harry tumbling on grass and catching the Golden Snitch
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: CRITICAL MISMATCH: Narration discusses the Sorting Hat honouring Harry's house choice, but the rendered visual is Harry catching the Golden Snitch on the Quidditch pitch. Completely unrelated sporting event.

test_cases.title: Known Positive - Harry Catches Golden Snitch in Quidditch
test_cases.claim: During his first Quidditch match, Harry Potter caught the Golden Snitch to win the game.
test_cases.expected_action: Harry Potter catches and displays the Golden Snitch
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: Direct positive alignment: Harry Potter in Quidditch attire catches and presents the Golden Snitch on the field.

test_cases.title: Same Character Wrong Event - Harry Wand Selection vs Quidditch Catch Claim
test_cases.claim: Harry Potter is flying on his broomstick chasing the Golden Snitch during a Quidditch match.
test_cases.expected_action: Harry being handed a wand in a shop
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: Harry Potter is clearly present, but the visible action is choosing a wand in Ollivanders shop, NOT flying on a broomstick or chasing a Golden Snitch.

test_cases.title: Correct Event - McGonagall Places Sorting Hat on Harry
test_cases.claim: Professor McGonagall places the ancient Sorting Hat onto Harry Potter's head during the sorting ceremony.
test_cases.expected_action: McGonagall lowers the Sorting Hat onto Harry's head
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: Direct positive alignment: Professor McGonagall lowers the pointed Sorting Hat onto Harry's head in front of the Great Hall.

test_cases.title: Non-Visual Internal Claim - Hat Senses Voldemort Soul Fragment
test_cases.claim: The Sorting Hat sensed Harry Potter's secret internal thoughts and the hidden soul fragment of Lord Voldemort.
test_cases.expected_action: Harry sitting quietly with the hat on his head
test_cases.ground_truth_rationale: While Harry wearing the hat is visible, internal mental thoughts and metaphysical soul fragments cannot be visually verified by camera frames. An editorial auditor must distinguish physical appearance from unverified internal lore.
